basis: Defined by mesoaxial polydactyly and congenital cardiac malformations; intellectual disability frequency is unspecified.
CTNNA3-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy affects ventricular myocardium and cardiac conduction.
Inherited fibrinolytic bleeding disorder; bruising does not establish lasting skin damage; intracranial and gastrointestinal bleeding occur in 5-29%.
Spastic cerebellar and pyramidal disease; bladder dysfunction (9/24) does not establish direct urinary injury; weakness and nystagmus are neurologic.
Mixed phenotype acute leukemia is a malignant disease of hematopoietic cells; leukemia alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Primary cervical carcinoma is reproductive; intestinal terminology describes histologic resemblance, not gastrointestinal origin.
Primary brain calcification with basal ganglia degeneration and neurologic dysfunction; localized calcification does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Cancer arises in the esophagus and stomach, both gastrointestinal organs.
Hereditary photodermatosis with cutaneous photosensitivity, dryness, freckling and pigmentation abnormalities.
Forebrain malformation; microphthalmia and cleft lip each 2/4 support eye and oral involvement. Nasal morphology lacks established dysfunction; panhypopituitarism 1/8.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the seminal vesicle, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Mitochondrial neurodegeneration; optic atrophy 5/6 and hearing loss 11/14. Cap excludes muscle atrophy 7/10 and cardiomyopathy 5/14, favoring more frequent sensory damage.
MET-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment in 9/9 patients.
Benign cartilaginous tumor arising in a phalanx.
Defined as EYA4-related nonsyndromic hearing loss; other EYA4-associated syndromes do not establish cardiac involvement here.
Spastic paraplegia with neuropathy and defining intervertebral disc herniation (80-99%); cataract and glaucoma occur in 5-29%.
5p deletion spectrum, including cri-du-chat syndrome, is principally characterized by developmental delay and intellectual disability; other organ defects vary.
Inherited lipid metabolism disorder; atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and pancreatitis are separately diagnosed complications.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Human papillomavirus infection; cutaneous, oral and genital sites vary, and persistent damaging lesions are not established in most infections.
Occupational asthma affects the bronchi; most cases involve immune sensitization, although irritant-induced forms also occur.
Inherited cerebellar ataxia with extrapyramidal motor dysfunction.
Congenital elbow synostosis; upper urinary tract/ureter anomalies and cavernous hemangiomas are each annotated at 80-99%, supporting renal and vascular involvement.
Sterol transport disorder; hemolysis and macrothrombocytopenia affect the annotated patient (1/1), with uncertain population frequency. Atherosclerosis is separately diagnosed.
Paget-cell neoplasm involving epidermal tissues, particularly extramammary skin; this definition concerns carcinoma rather than Paget disease of bone.
